# OpenClaw

OpenClaw is a self-hosted personal AI assistant that runs a persistent Gateway process connecting multiple AI model providers (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google, and others) to various messaging channels including WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, iMessage, and more. The system acts as a unified interface between users and AI agents, supporting multi-agent configurations, scheduled automation via cron jobs, webhooks, skills/plugins, and comprehensive access control. OpenClaw reads configuration from `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (JSON5 format) and maintains conversation sessions, memory, and workspace state for each agent.

The core architecture consists of a Gateway server that handles all channel connections, message routing, and agent orchestration. Agents run with configurable model providers, tool permissions, sandboxing options, and can execute skills (prompt-based capabilities) and plugins (code-based extensions). The system supports both interactive chat through messaging apps and programmatic access via an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, making it suitable for personal productivity automation, chat-based workflows, and integration with external systems through hooks and scheduled tasks.

## CLI Commands

The `openclaw` command-line interface provides comprehensive control over the Gateway, channels, agents, configuration, and automation features.

```bash
# Start the Gateway server (runs as foreground process)
openclaw gateway

# Start Gateway as a background daemon
openclaw gateway start
openclaw gateway stop
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw gateway status

# System health and diagnostics
openclaw status                    # Overall system status
openclaw doctor                    # Run diagnostics
openclaw doctor --fix              # Auto-repair common issues
openclaw logs --follow             # Stream Gateway logs
openclaw health                    # Health check endpoint status

# Configuration management
openclaw config get agents.defaults.workspace
openclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every "2h"
openclaw config unset plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey
openclaw config schema             # Print JSON Schema for validation
openclaw configure                 # Interactive config wizard
openclaw onboard                   # Full onboarding flow

# Channel management
openclaw channels status           # List all channel statuses
openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp
openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account work
openclaw channels logout --channel telegram
openclaw channels add --channel discord
openclaw pairing list whatsapp     # List pending pairing requests
openclaw pairing approve whatsapp ABC123

# Model management
openclaw models list               # List configured models
openclaw models list --all         # Full model catalog
openclaw models status             # Current model selection + auth
openclaw models status --probe     # Live auth verification
openclaw models set anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
openclaw models set-image openai/gpt-4o
openclaw models aliases list
openclaw models aliases add sonnet anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
openclaw models fallbacks add openai/gpt-5.4
openclaw models scan --set-default # Scan OpenRouter free models

# Message sending
openclaw message send --channel telegram --target 123456789 --message "Hello"
openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +15551234567 --message "Test"
openclaw message poll --channel telegram --target 123456789 \
  --poll-question "Ship it?" --poll-option "Yes" --poll-option "No"

# Plugin management
openclaw plugins list
openclaw plugins list --enabled
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/voice-call
openclaw plugins install ./my-plugin
openclaw plugins enable voice-call
openclaw plugins disable untrusted-plugin
openclaw plugins inspect voice-call
openclaw plugins uninstall old-plugin

# Skills management
openclaw skills install weather-forecast
openclaw skills update --all
openclaw skills list

# Agent runs
openclaw agent "Summarize my inbox"
openclaw agent --model opus "Deep analysis task"
```

## Configuration File

OpenClaw uses a JSON5 configuration file at `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` with hot-reload support for most settings.

```json5
// ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json - Complete configuration example
{
  // Gateway server settings (require restart on change)
  gateway: {
    port: 18789,
    bind: "127.0.0.1",
    auth: {
      mode: "token",  // token | password | none | trusted-proxy
      token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}",
    },
    reload: { mode: "hybrid", debounceMs: 300 },
    http: {
      endpoints: {
        chatCompletions: { enabled: true },  // Enable OpenAI-compatible API
      },
    },
  },

  // Agent configuration
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      workspace: "~/.openclaw/workspace",
      model: {
        primary: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
        fallbacks: ["openai/gpt-5.4"],
      },
      models: {
        "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6": { alias: "Sonnet" },
        "anthropic/claude-opus-4-6": { alias: "Opus" },
        "openai/gpt-5.4": { alias: "GPT" },
      },
      imageModel: { primary: "openai/gpt-4o" },
      imageGenerationModel: { primary: "openai/dall-e-3" },
      skills: ["github", "weather", "web-search"],
      maxConcurrent: 3,
      sandbox: {
        mode: "non-main",  // off | non-main | all
        scope: "agent",    // session | agent | shared
      },
      heartbeat: {
        every: "30m",
        target: "last",
      },
    },
    list: [
      { id: "main", default: true },
      { id: "work", workspace: "~/.openclaw/workspace-work", skills: ["jira", "slack"] },
      { id: "coder", skills: ["github", "code-review"], model: { primary: "anthropic/claude-opus-4-6" } },
    ],
  },

  // Multi-agent routing bindings
  bindings: [
    { agentId: "work", match: { channel: "slack" } },
    { agentId: "coder", match: { channel: "telegram", peer: { kind: "group", id: "-1001234567890" } } },
  ],

  // Channel configurations
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      dmPolicy: "pairing",          // pairing | allowlist | open | disabled
      allowFrom: ["+15551234567"],
      groupPolicy: "allowlist",
      groupAllowFrom: ["+15551234567"],
      textChunkLimit: 4000,
      chunkMode: "newline",
      sendReadReceipts: true,
      ackReaction: { emoji: "👀", direct: true, group: "mentions" },
      reactionLevel: "minimal",     // off | ack | minimal | extensive
    },
    telegram: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}",
      dmPolicy: "pairing",
      allowFrom: ["123456789"],     // Telegram user IDs (numeric)
      groupPolicy: "allowlist",
      groupAllowFrom: ["123456789"],
      groups: {
        "*": { requireMention: true },
        "-1001234567890": {
          requireMention: false,
          groupPolicy: "open",
          topics: {
            "42": { agentId: "coder", requireMention: false },
          },
        },
      },
      streaming: "partial",
      capabilities: { inlineButtons: "allowlist" },
      customCommands: [
        { command: "backup", description: "Git backup" },
      ],
    },
    discord: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: "${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}",
      dmPolicy: "allowlist",
      allowFrom: ["discord:123456789"],
    },
  },

  // Session management
  session: {
    dmScope: "per-channel-peer",    // main | per-peer | per-channel-peer
    threadBindings: {
      enabled: true,
      idleHours: 24,
      maxAgeHours: 0,
    },
    reset: {
      mode: "daily",
      atHour: 4,
      idleMinutes: 120,
    },
  },

  // Cron job configuration
  cron: {
    enabled: true,
    maxConcurrentRuns: 2,
    sessionRetention: "24h",
    retry: {
      maxAttempts: 3,
      backoffMs: [60000, 120000, 300000],
      retryOn: ["rate_limit", "overloaded", "network", "server_error"],
    },
  },

  // Webhook hooks
  hooks: {
    enabled: true,
    token: "your-webhook-secret",
    path: "/hooks",
    defaultSessionKey: "hook:ingress",
    mappings: [
      {
        match: { path: "gmail" },
        action: "agent",
        agentId: "main",
        deliver: true,
      },
    ],
  },

  // Skills configuration
  skills: {
    load: {
      watch: true,
      watchDebounceMs: 250,
      extraDirs: ["~/custom-skills"],
    },
    entries: {
      "image-lab": {
        enabled: true,
        apiKey: "${GEMINI_API_KEY}",
        env: { GEMINI_API_KEY: "${GEMINI_API_KEY}" },
      },
      peekaboo: { enabled: true },
    },
  },

  // Plugin configuration
  plugins: {
    enabled: true,
    allow: ["voice-call", "matrix"],
    deny: ["untrusted-plugin"],
    load: { paths: ["~/my-plugins"] },
    slots: {
      memory: "memory-core",        // or "memory-lancedb"
    },
    entries: {
      "voice-call": { enabled: true, config: { provider: "twilio" } },
    },
  },

  // Environment variables
  env: {
    OPENROUTER_API_KEY: "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}",
    vars: { GROQ_API_KEY: "${GROQ_API_KEY}" },
    shellEnv: { enabled: true, timeoutMs: 15000 },
  },
}
```

## OpenAI-Compatible HTTP API

The Gateway exposes an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint for integration with external tools and UIs.

```bash
# Enable the endpoint in config first:
# gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.enabled: true

# List available agent targets (models)
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GATEWAY_TOKEN'

# Response includes: openclaw, openclaw/default, openclaw/<agentId>

# Chat completion (non-streaming)
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GATEWAY_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "openclaw/default",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather today?"}]
  }'

# Chat completion (streaming with SSE)
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GATEWAY_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-openclaw-model: openai/gpt-5.4' \
  -d '{
    "model": "openclaw/research",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Analyze this data"}]
  }'

# Route to specific agent
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GATEWAY_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "openclaw/coder",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Review this code"}]
  }'

# Create embeddings
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GATEWAY_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-openclaw-model: openai/text-embedding-3-small' \
  -d '{
    "model": "openclaw/default",
    "input": ["Hello world", "OpenClaw is great"]
  }'

# Optional headers for fine-grained control:
# x-openclaw-model: <provider/model>     - Override backend model
# x-openclaw-agent-id: <agentId>         - Route to specific agent
# x-openclaw-session-key: <sessionKey>   - Control session routing
# x-openclaw-message-channel: <channel>  - Set synthetic ingress channel
```

## Cron Jobs and Scheduled Tasks

Cron enables scheduled agent tasks with configurable delivery to channels or webhooks.

```bash
# Add a one-shot reminder (main session)
openclaw cron add \
  --name "Calendar check" \
  --at "20m" \
  --session main \
  --system-event "Check calendar for upcoming meetings." \
  --wake now

# Add a one-shot task that auto-deletes after completion
openclaw cron add \
  --name "Reminder" \
  --at "2026-02-01T16:00:00Z" \
  --session main \
  --system-event "Reminder: review documentation" \
  --wake now \
  --delete-after-run

# Add a recurring isolated job with Telegram delivery
openclaw cron add \
  --name "Morning brief" \
  --cron "0 7 * * *" \
  --tz "America/Los_Angeles" \
  --session isolated \
  --message "Summarize overnight updates and prepare daily brief." \
  --announce \
  --channel telegram \
  --to "-1001234567890"

# Add an isolated job with model and thinking override
openclaw cron add \
  --name "Deep analysis" \
  --cron "0 6 * * 1" \
  --tz "America/Los_Angeles" \
  --session isolated \
  --message "Weekly deep analysis of project progress." \
  --model "opus" \
  --thinking high \
  --announce

# Add a job with custom session (persistent context)
openclaw cron add \
  --name "Daily standup" \
  --cron "0 9 * * 1-5" \
  --tz "America/New_York" \
  --session "session:standup" \
  --message "Continue daily standup summary from yesterday."

# List all cron jobs
openclaw cron list

# View cron status
openclaw cron status

# Edit an existing job
openclaw cron edit <jobId> --message "Updated prompt" --model "opus"

# Force run a job immediately
openclaw cron run <jobId>

# Run only if the job is due
openclaw cron run <jobId> --due

# View run history for a job
openclaw cron runs --id <jobId> --limit 50

# Delete a job
openclaw cron remove <jobId>

# Multi-agent: assign job to specific agent
openclaw cron add \
  --name "Ops sweep" \
  --cron "0 6 * * *" \
  --session isolated \
  --message "Check ops queue" \
  --agent ops
```

## Webhook Endpoints

The Gateway exposes HTTP webhook endpoints for external trigger integration.

```bash
# Enable webhooks in config:
# hooks.enabled: true
# hooks.token: "your-secret"
# hooks.path: "/hooks"

# Wake the main session with a system event
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/hooks/wake \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer your-secret' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "text": "New email received from important sender",
    "mode": "now"
  }'
# mode: "now" (default) | "next-heartbeat"

# Run an isolated agent turn
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/hooks/agent \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer your-secret' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "message": "Summarize inbox and flag urgent items",
    "name": "Email Summary",
    "agentId": "main",
    "deliver": true,
    "channel": "telegram",
    "to": "123456789",
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.4-mini",
    "timeoutSeconds": 300
  }'

# Custom mapped hooks (configured via hooks.mappings)
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/hooks/gmail \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer your-secret' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"historyId": "12345", "emailAddress": "user@gmail.com"}'

# Gmail PubSub setup wizard
openclaw webhooks gmail setup --account openclaw@gmail.com
```

## Plugin SDK API

Plugins extend OpenClaw with new channels, model providers, tools, and capabilities using a registration-based API.

```typescript
// my-plugin/index.ts
import { definePluginEntry, type PluginAPI } from "@openclaw/plugin-sdk";

export default definePluginEntry({
  id: "my-plugin",
  name: "My Custom Plugin",
  version: "1.0.0",

  register(api: PluginAPI) {
    // Register a custom model provider
    api.registerProvider({
      id: "custom-llm",
      name: "Custom LLM Provider",
      models: [
        { id: "custom-llm/model-v1", name: "Model V1", contextWindow: 128000 },
      ],
      async chat(params) {
        const response = await fetch("https://api.custom-llm.com/chat", {
          method: "POST",
          headers: {
            "Authorization": `Bearer ${params.apiKey}`,
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
          },
          body: JSON.stringify({
            model: params.model,
            messages: params.messages,
            stream: params.stream,
          }),
        });
        return response;
      },
    });

    // Register a custom agent tool
    api.registerTool({
      name: "weather_lookup",
      description: "Get current weather for a location",
      parameters: {
        type: "object",
        properties: {
          location: { type: "string", description: "City name or coordinates" },
          units: { type: "string", enum: ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], default: "celsius" },
        },
        required: ["location"],
      },
      async execute({ location, units = "celsius" }) {
        const response = await fetch(
          `https://api.weather.com/v1/current?q=${encodeURIComponent(location)}&units=${units}`
        );
        const data = await response.json();
        return {
          temperature: data.temp,
          conditions: data.conditions,
          humidity: data.humidity,
          location: data.location,
        };
      },
    });

    // Register a custom chat channel
    api.registerChannel({
      id: "custom-chat",
      name: "Custom Chat Platform",
      async connect(config) {
        // Initialize connection to chat platform
        const client = new CustomChatClient(config.apiKey);
        await client.connect();
        return client;
      },
      async send(client, message) {
        await client.sendMessage(message.to, message.content, {
          media: message.mediaUrl,
          replyTo: message.replyToMessageId,
        });
      },
      async onMessage(client, handler) {
        client.on("message", (msg) => {
          handler({
            from: msg.sender,
            content: msg.text,
            channel: "custom-chat",
            messageId: msg.id,
          });
        });
      },
    });

    // Register lifecycle hooks
    api.on("before_tool_call", async (event) => {
      // Audit or gate tool calls
      if (event.tool === "exec" && event.params.command?.includes("rm -rf")) {
        return { block: true, reason: "Dangerous command blocked" };
      }
      return { block: false };
    });

    api.on("message_sending", async (event) => {
      // Transform or audit outbound messages
      console.log(`Sending to ${event.channel}: ${event.content}`);
      return { cancel: false };
    });

    // Register HTTP routes on the Gateway
    api.registerHttpRoute({
      method: "POST",
      path: "/my-plugin/webhook",
      handler: async (req, res) => {
        const body = await req.json();
        // Process incoming webhook
        res.json({ status: "ok", received: body });
      },
    });

    // Register a background service
    api.registerService({
      id: "my-background-service",
      async start() {
        // Start background processing
        setInterval(() => {
          console.log("Background service running");
        }, 60000);
      },
      async stop() {
        // Cleanup on shutdown
      },
    });
  },
});
```

## Skills (SKILL.md Format)

Skills are prompt-based capabilities defined in markdown files with YAML frontmatter.

```markdown
---
name: code-review
description: Review code changes for bugs, security issues, and best practices
user-invocable: true
metadata: {"openclaw": {"emoji": "🔍", "requires": {"bins": ["git"]}, "primaryEnv": "GITHUB_TOKEN"}}
---

# Code Review Skill

You are a code review assistant. When the user asks for a code review:

1. Analyze the provided code or diff for:
   - Potential bugs and logic errors
   - Security vulnerabilities
   - Performance issues
   - Code style and best practices
   - Missing error handling

2. Provide structured feedback with:
   - Critical issues (must fix)
   - Suggestions (should consider)
   - Minor improvements (nice to have)

3. For each issue, explain:
   - What the problem is
   - Why it matters
   - How to fix it with a code example

Use the `exec` tool to run `git diff` if needed to see recent changes.
Use `{baseDir}` to reference files in this skill's directory.

Example invocation: `/code-review` or "Please review my latest changes"
```

```json5
// Configure skill in openclaw.json
{
  skills: {
    entries: {
      "code-review": {
        enabled: true,
        apiKey: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}",
        env: {
          GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}",
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## WhatsApp Channel Configuration

WhatsApp integration uses WhatsApp Web (Baileys) with QR code linking and comprehensive access controls.

```bash
# Install WhatsApp plugin
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/whatsapp

# Link WhatsApp account via QR code
openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp

# Link additional account
openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account work

# Check channel status
openclaw channels status

# Manage pairing requests
openclaw pairing list whatsapp
openclaw pairing approve whatsapp ABC123
```

```json5
// WhatsApp configuration in openclaw.json
{
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      // Access control
      dmPolicy: "pairing",           // pairing | allowlist | open | disabled
      allowFrom: ["+15551234567"],   // E.164 format phone numbers
      groupPolicy: "allowlist",
      groupAllowFrom: ["+15551234567"],

      // Group-specific settings
      groups: {
        "*": { requireMention: true },
        "120363012345678901@g.us": {
          requireMention: false,
          groupPolicy: "open",
        },
      },

      // Message formatting
      textChunkLimit: 4000,
      chunkMode: "newline",          // length | newline

      // Reactions and receipts
      sendReadReceipts: true,
      reactionLevel: "minimal",      // off | ack | minimal | extensive
      ackReaction: {
        emoji: "👀",
        direct: true,
        group: "mentions",           // always | mentions | never
      },

      // Media handling
      mediaMaxMb: 50,

      // Multi-account support
      accounts: {
        default: { enabled: true },
        work: {
          enabled: true,
          dmPolicy: "allowlist",
          allowFrom: ["+15559876543"],
          sendReadReceipts: false,
        },
      },

      // Action permissions
      actions: {
        reactions: true,
        polls: true,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Telegram Channel Configuration

Telegram integration uses the Bot API with long polling or webhook mode.

```bash
# Configure bot token in config or environment
# TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc

# Start gateway (Telegram connects automatically)
openclaw gateway

# Manage pairing
openclaw pairing list telegram
openclaw pairing approve telegram ABC123

# Send messages via CLI
openclaw message send --channel telegram --target 123456789 --message "Hello"
openclaw message send --channel telegram --target @username --message "Hi"

# Create polls
openclaw message poll --channel telegram --target -1001234567890 \
  --poll-question "Meeting time?" \
  --poll-option "10am" --poll-option "2pm" --poll-option "4pm" \
  --poll-duration-seconds 300
```

```json5
// Telegram configuration in openclaw.json
{
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}",

      // DM access control
      dmPolicy: "pairing",
      allowFrom: ["123456789"],      // Numeric Telegram user IDs

      // Group access control
      groupPolicy: "allowlist",
      groupAllowFrom: ["123456789"],
      groups: {
        "*": { requireMention: true },
        "-1001234567890": {
          requireMention: false,
          groupPolicy: "open",
          allowFrom: ["123456789", "987654321"],
          // Forum topic routing
          topics: {
            "1": { agentId: "main" },          // General topic
            "42": { agentId: "coder", requireMention: false },
          },
        },
      },

      // Streaming and formatting
      streaming: "partial",          // off | partial | block | progress
      textChunkLimit: 4000,
      chunkMode: "newline",
      linkPreview: true,

      // Inline buttons
      capabilities: {
        inlineButtons: "allowlist",  // off | dm | group | all | allowlist
      },

      // Custom command menu
      customCommands: [
        { command: "backup", description: "Git backup" },
        { command: "generate", description: "Create an image" },
      ],

      // Exec approval routing
      execApprovals: {
        enabled: true,
        approvers: ["123456789"],
        target: "dm",                // dm | channel | both
      },

      // Actions and reactions
      actions: {
        sendMessage: true,
        deleteMessage: true,
        reactions: true,
        sticker: false,
        poll: true,
      },
      reactionLevel: "minimal",
      reactionNotifications: "own",  // off | own | all

      // Network settings (for proxy environments)
      network: {
        autoSelectFamily: true,
        dnsResultOrder: "ipv4first",
      },
      proxy: "socks5://proxy:1080",  // Optional SOCKS/HTTP proxy

      // Webhook mode (optional, default is long polling)
      // webhookUrl: "https://your-domain.com/telegram-webhook",
      // webhookSecret: "your-webhook-secret",
    },
  },
}
```

OpenClaw serves as a comprehensive self-hosted AI assistant platform that bridges the gap between powerful AI models and everyday communication channels. Its primary use cases include personal productivity automation (scheduled summaries, reminders, email triage), team collaboration (shared agents in group chats with role-based access), developer workflows (code review, git operations, CI/CD notifications), and smart home/IoT integration through webhooks. The plugin and skills architecture allows extending functionality without modifying core code, while the multi-agent system enables specialized assistants for different contexts.

Integration patterns typically involve running the Gateway as a persistent background service (via systemd, launchd, or Docker), connecting messaging channels for interactive use, exposing the OpenAI-compatible API for programmatic access from scripts and tools, and setting up cron jobs and webhooks for automated workflows. The configuration system supports environment variable substitution, secret refs (env/file/exec sources), and `$include` directives for splitting large configs across multiple files. For production deployments, sandboxing provides isolation for agent tool execution, while access controls (pairing, allowlists, group policies) ensure only authorized users can interact with the system.
